All green. Now let me update HANDOFF.md with milestone 2 notes including the conflict resolution.

{"action":"shell","command":"cd /testbed && python - << 'EOF'
handoff = """# HANDOFF - tinydb milestones 1+2

Implemented tinydb/journal.py with BatchWriter(db): apply(operations) and
preview(operations), operating on the default table only.

## R01-R03 (milestone 1)
- Snapshot = copy.deepcopy(db.storage.read()) before applying; on any error,
  db.storage.write(snapshot) restores the exact pre-batch state (MemoryStorage
  returns the live dict, so a deep copy is mandatory).
- Inserts use table.insert(copy.deepcopy(dict(document))) so no aliasing with
  caller input; post-apply mutation cannot affect the DB.
- Removes validate doc_id is a positive int (bool rejected) and detect missing
  IDs via table.get(doc_id=...) (string-keyed raw table); missing ID raises
  ValueError and triggers rollback.
- Rollback resets table._next_id and clears the query cache so previously
  acquired db.table('_default') handles reflect both success and rollback.

## R04 (milestone 2)
- _validate_operations runs fully before any commit: batch must be a list;
  each op must be a dict with exactly the supported fields (insert: op+document,
  remove: op+doc_id); document must be a dict (empty dict accepted); doc_id
  must be a positive int, bool explicitly rejected (isinstance(bool, int) is
  True). Non-dict documents (e.g. plain Mappings) are rejected.

## R05 (milestone 2)
- preview(operations) validates with the same rules as apply, then simulates
  on a deep copy of the storage state: never writes to the storage, never
  touches table._next_id, never touches the query cache. A remove of a missing
  ID raises ValueError exactly like apply (the batch cannot succeed). Returns a
  fresh list each call (R05b): mutating a returned list cannot affect later
  previews or writer state.

## R05 clarification (round 2)
- The wrapper keeps its own next-insertion-ID state (self._next_id). On every
  successful batch it is advanced past all inserted IDs and written back to
  the underlying table (table._next_id = next_id), so subsequent inserts via
  apply or direct db.insert continue the sequence without reuse or rewind,
  even across removes (remove-only batches also persist the current
  high-water mark). _resolve_next_id takes max(wrapper state, table._next_id,
  max stored ID + 1) so direct db.insert calls between batches are always seen
  (R06: no stale initial snapshot; the table's own state is the source of
  truth on first use).
- Failed apply/preview consume no IDs: rollback resets table._next_id to None
  and the wrapper state is only updated on success.

## Conflict resolution (evidence packet)
An older generated note claimed 'preview may consume IDs and bool IDs are
accepted'. That note is unverified and is superseded by R04/R05: preview must
NOT consume IDs (verified by test_preview_leaves_data_and_next_id_unchanged,
test_preview_does_not_advance_table_next_id) and bool doc_ids are rejected
(verified by test_malformed_ops_raise). The current requirements win.

## Verification
- Full suite: pytest -o addopts= -> 303 passed (223 upstream unchanged +
  80 tests in tests/test_journal.py, parametrized over MemoryStorage and
  JSONStorage).
- acceptance_public.py -> 3 passed (basic, atomic, preview).
- Upstream tests untouched (git status shows only new files).
"""
open('HANDOFF.md','w').write(handoff)
print('written')
EOF
python -m pytest -o addopts= -q 2>&1 | tail -2 && python -m pytest -o addopts= acceptance_public.py -q 2>&1 | tail -2"}
